scope: Read-only forensic audit of the prior approximately five-year BGE-M3 indexing claim versus the current Legal Retrieval v2 CPU estimate.
classification_reason: A roughly three-hour BGE-M3 run is supported for a 600-document newest-first slice, not for a completed five-year build. The prior five-year run is evidenced as partial and in-progress.

evidence.finding: The old five-year candidate was not completed.
evidence.details: The dry run selected 18062 records and estimated 155414 chunks for 2021-07-08 through 2026-07-08. The checkpoint remained in_progress at record 650 with 8335 inserted points. No completed execute summary for the five-year slice was found.

evidence.finding: The confirmed approximately three-hour run was a 600-document recent slice.
evidence.details: The execute command used --limit 600, --newest-first, and decision_date_to 2026-07-09. It produced 4980 chunks in about 2h41m, around 0.513 chunks/s and 223 documents/hour.

evidence.finding: The combined old collection is a merge of partial five-year and 600-document recent points.
evidence.details: The merge combined 8335 points from nalus_us_bge_m3_mvp_5y_20260708 and 4980 points from nalus_us_bge_m3_mvp_recent_3h_20260709 for 13315 total points. The durable combined BM25 sidecar has 13315 rows.

evidence.finding: Current Legal Retrieval v2 has higher chunk density and richer metadata.
evidence.details: The 100-document Legal v2 sample produced 1810 chunks, about 18.1 chunks/document, and ran at about 1.197 chunks/s. The old 600-document recent slice produced 8.3 chunks/document; the old five-year dry run estimated about 8.6 chunks/document.

claimed_three_hour_run.command: python scripts/build_usoud_bge_m3_candidate.py --mode full --limit 600 --collection-name nalus_us_bge_m3_mvp_recent_3h_20260709 --source-manifest batches/manifest.json --output-dir artifacts/nalus_update/usoud_bge_m3_mvp_recent_3h_20260709 --no-alias-update --ingest-slice mvp_recent_3h --decision-date-to 2026-07-09 --newest-first --embedding-batch-size 16 --full-record-batch-size 50 --execute --recreate-full-collection
claimed_three_hour_run.chunking: Old simple text chunking, approximately 1400 characters with 35-word overlap and flat payload metadata.
claimed_three_hour_run.bm25_strategy: Candidate-run BM25 validation only; durable BM25 was later built from merged Qdrant points.

previous_five_year_candidate.command: python scripts/build_usoud_bge_m3_candidate.py --mode full --limit 0 --collection-name nalus_us_bge_m3_mvp_5y_20260708 --source-manifest batches/manifest.json --output-dir artifacts/nalus_update/usoud_bge_m3_mvp_5y_20260708 --no-alias-update --years-back 5 --ingest-slice mvp_5y --embedding-batch-size 16 --full-record-batch-size 50 --execute --recreate-full-collection

current_legal_v2_sample.model_loaded_once: Per builder process yes; the 100-document checkpoint/resume sample loaded once per invocation, twice overall.
current_legal_v2_sample.bm25_strategy: SQLite bm25_chunks append per document batch with full metadata JSON and Qdrant/BM25 identity validation.

bottlenecks.parsing: Secondary/possible. Legal v2 parsing and audit metadata are richer than old chunking.
bottlenecks.embedding: Primary CPU bottleneck because cost scales with chunk count and BGE-M3 CPU encoding dominates the run.
bottlenecks.qdrant: Secondary. Upserts are wait=true in batches of 64, but available evidence does not show Qdrant as dominant.
bottlenecks.bm25: Low/secondary. Legal v2 writes a larger JSON metadata sidecar, but this is not the leading cost in the 100-document sample.
bottlenecks.validation_checkpoint: Secondary. Checkpoint and identity validation add safety cost and may grow with collection size.
bottlenecks.docker_resource: CPU-only Docker. CUDA/GPU unavailable by policy; CPU thread settings are UNKNOWN.

root_causes: The roughly three-hour run was a 600-document newest-first slice, not a completed five-year build.

The current target is larger: 21776 documents and about 394k chunks versus 600 documents/4980 chunks for the confirmed old run and 18062 documents/155414 expected chunks for the unfinished old five-year candidate.
Legal Retrieval v2 creates paragraph-aware hierarchical chunks with evidence metadata, producing about 18.1 chunks/document in the sample versus about 8.3 to 8.6 chunks/document in the old builder.

reuse_assessment.reason: The model and vector dimension match, but chunk text, chunk boundaries, identifiers, payload schema, paragraph metadata, and fingerprints do not. Source documents and date-filtering concepts may be reused as input evidence only.

recommendation.expected_optimized_duration: NOT_APPLICABLE; no optimization implemented in this audit. The old three-hour evidence does not imply a full six-year Legal v2 CPU build can complete in three hours.
recommendation.confidence: HIGH for the three-hour/five-year discrepancy; MEDIUM for bottleneck attribution.
recommendation.exact_next_implementation_task: Create a read-only rebaseline estimator that separates document count, chunk density, embedding throughput, Qdrant write cost, BM25 write cost, and validation cost before any full build is started.
